blurb: Where the Terabase team is staying, in the middle of the Strip next to Harrah's and the Flamingo. The LINQ Promenade is an outdoor walkway of casual restaurants and bars leading to the High Roller wheel. Best for team breakfasts before heading to the show and relaxed team dinners afterward. Too far for lunch from Central Hall.
f1: The LINQ fronts the Strip section of the race circuit. On Thu 11/19, expect closures and crowds from early afternoon (2025 closures began about 1pm). Use the Monorail, not a car.
getThere: Monorail from the LVCC (Boingo) station to Harrah's/The LINQ: one stop, trains every 4–8 min, $6.25 a ride. It runs 24 hours from Tue 11/17 to Mon 11/23 for F1 week. RE+ lists Harrah's/LINQ as Monorail hotels; confirm whether a show shuttle also stops there. Allow about 25 min from the booth, 40 at show close.
name: Center Strip: The LINQ and the Promenade (team hotel)
whoStays: The Terabase team; mostly leisure travelers, fewer customers

blurb: Inside the convention center. Counter-service food only, so use it for quick team lunches, not customer meals.
name: LVCC campus

blurb: The big Strip resorts nearest LVCC, on the West Hall side of the campus. Many customers and senior guests stay here. Upscale, reservable restaurants that suit customer dinners, and hotel breakfasts that work if the customer is staying in the same resort.
f1: Wynn/Encore sits just north of the circuit's Sands Ave turn. On Thu 11/19, expect Strip closures and gridlock from early afternoon. The Loop runs underground, so use it instead of a car. Resorts World and Fontainebleau are farther north but still see heavy traffic.
getThere: Walk about 18–27 min from the Central Hall doors (Encore and Resorts World across the Strip; Fontainebleau via West Hall), or ride the Vegas Loop: Fontainebleau free, Encore and Resorts World $4.25.
name: North Strip resorts: Wynn/Encore, Resorts World, Fontainebleau, Circus Circus
whoStays: Customers, partners and executives who prefer a Strip resort

blurb: A cluster of business hotels facing the convention center on Paradise Rd: the Renaissance, Courtyard, Las Vegas Marriott and, a little farther south, Embassy Suites. No casino floors, quieter, and the shortest walk to Central Hall. Good for working breakfasts and relaxed dinners.
f1: Outside the race circuit. Expect normal convention traffic.
getThere: Walk, about 4–12 min from the Central Hall doors
name: Paradise Road, across from Central Hall
whoStays: Exhibitors and attendees who want to walk to the show

blurb: The large casino resort directly next to LVCC. Several restaurants under one roof, from a casual café to a steakhouse, and the easiest place to grab a walk-in lunch.
getThere: Walk about 7 min (estimate), or the Vegas Loop from the Westgate station at the hotel entrance ($4.25 one way)
name: Westgate, next door to the north
whoStays: Many show attendees; it is the closest full resort

blurb: The SAHARA sits at the north end of the Monorail, one stop past the Westgate and next door to the Fontainebleau. A good mid-to-upscale dinner cluster with private rooms; breakfast choices are thin.
f1: Well north of the race circuit. Expect normal convention traffic.
getThere: Monorail from LVCC (Boingo) to SAHARA: 2 stops, about 4 min, trains every 4–8 min, $6.25. A bridge over the Strip leads into SAHARA's second level. Allow about 25 min from the booth, 40 at show close.
name: North end: SAHARA
whoStays: Attendees wanting a newer, mid-priced resort near LVCC

blurb: Large resorts around the Flamingo Rd and Strip corner, one stop past The LINQ. The Flamingo is closest to the station. Caesars Palace is across the Strip and a long walk inside. The Cromwell was renamed The Vanderpump Hotel in May 2026.
f1: The Flamingo side is on the Strip section of the circuit. Expect closures and crowds from early afternoon Thu 11/19; Monorail runs 24 hours Nov 17–23. Book customer dinners Tue or Wed if you can.
getThere: Monorail from LVCC to Flamingo/Caesars Palace: 2 stops, about 5 min, $6.25. The station is behind the Flamingo. Allow 5–10 min to Flamingo restaurants and 15–25 min to Caesars Palace restaurants after you get off.
name: Center Strip: Flamingo, Caesars Palace and The Vanderpump Hotel
whoStays: Many customers and executives; Caesars Palace is a popular conference hotel

blurb: Horseshoe (formerly Bally's) and Paris sit side by side on the Strip. Paris has the stronger restaurant lineup, including the Eiffel Tower Restaurant and Mon Ami Gabi. Horseshoe has no sit-down breakfast.
f1: Inside the race circuit. Thu 11/19 will be busy and pricier (the Eiffel Tower Restaurant has a special race menu Nov 19–21). Prefer Tue or Wed.
getThere: Monorail from LVCC to Horseshoe/Paris: 3 stops, about 7–10 min, $6.25. The station is at the back of Horseshoe; Paris is reached through an indoor connector, about 10–15 min.
name: Center Strip: Horseshoe and Paris
whoStays: Customers who want a central Strip location

blurb: The MGM Grand is the south end of the Monorail and one of the largest hotels in the city, with a deep restaurant row. Good for larger hosted dinners with private rooms.
f1: Just south of the circuit's Harmon Ave edge. Expect heavy traffic but no track closures at the hotel itself.
getThere: Monorail from LVCC to MGM Grand: 4 stops, about 9–12 min, $6.25. The station is at the back of the property; allow about 10 min to the restaurant row.
name: South end: MGM Grand

blurb: Standalone restaurants between Central Hall and the Strip, along Convention Center Dr: an old-Vegas Italian dining room, a classic deli, and the iconic Peppermill. No hotel needed.
getThere: Walk: cross Paradise Rd at Convention Center Dr and head west. Piero's is about 6 min from the doors; the Strip corner (Peppermill, Denny's) about 15–16 min.
name: Convention Center Drive and the Strip corner
whoStays: Anyone; these are not hotel restaurants
